name: securo
description: Open-source personal finance manager. Self-hosted, privacy-first.
readmeExcerpt:
Securo




Website · Demo · Roadmap · Docs · Discord · Talk to the maintainer

Finance apps want your data. This one doesn't.

We believe personal finance should actually be personal. No corporation should sit between you and your financial data. Securo is an open-source finance manager that runs on your own infrastructure, giving you full visibility into your accounts, spending, and habits, without surrendering a single byte to third parties. Take back control.

## Quick Start **Linux & macOS** (uses Docker or Podman; installs Docker if neither is present): ```bash curl -fsSL https://usesecuro.com/install.sh | bash ``` **Windows:** Install [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/), then: ```bash git clone https://github.com/securo-finance/securo.git && cd securo docker compose up --build ``` Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) and create an account. That's it.

## Features - Multi-account management with running balances - Transaction management with search, filters, and CSV export - File import (OFX, QIF, CAMT, CSV) - Auto-categorization rules engine - Recurring transactions, budgets, and loan/financing tracking - Goals and savings targets with progress tracking - Asset management with valuation tracking and growth rules - Reports: Net Worth and Income vs Expenses with category sparklines - Multi-currency support with automatic FX conversion - Multi-user support with workspaces, roles, and an admin panel - Passkeys, two-factor authentication (TOTP), and OIDC single sign-on - Bank sync via providers (Pluggy, Enable Banking, SimpleFIN, extensible) - AI Agents (optional): self-hosted LLM chat with tool-use over your data ### Reporting dates and bank balances Synchronized transactions can have a reporting-date override without changing the bank's booking date. Clear the override to restore automatic attribution; later bank syncs preserve the override. Reporting periods and transaction-list dates follow the override. Account running balances and posted cash-flow balance movements still follow the bank date (or the effective movement date in accrual mode). A posted expense attributed to a future period appears in that period's cash-flow outflow, but is not deducted from the projected balance a second time. Pending card rows retain their manually selected bill date for forecast outflow and projected balance timing, including in cash mode. The calendar offers separate reporting-date and bank-date views. Moved rows retain their original bank date in the transaction list. ## Optional capabilities Everything beyond the core is off by default, needs a single env flag, and costs nothing until you turn it on. Full setup guides live in the [documentation](https://docs.usesecuro.com/): - **Bank sync**: Pluggy for Brazilian banks, Enable Banking for ~2500 European PSD2 banks, and SimpleFIN for US and international banks. [Setup guides](https://docs.usesecuro.com/features/bank-sync/) - **Login & security**: passkeys (Touch ID, Face ID, security keys), TOTP two-factor, and OIDC single sign-on with account linking and provider role sync. [Guide](https://docs.usesecuro.com/features/security/) - **Exchange rates**: a free [Open Exchange Rates](https://openexchangerates.org/) key enables automatic currency conversion; without one, cross-currency amounts fall back to 1:1 with a visual warning. [Details](https://docs.usesecuro.com/deployment/docker/) - **Timezone**: balances, budgets, and due dates turn over at midnight in your application timezone, set once in Admin Settings, with per-workspace overrides. [Details](https://docs.usesecuro.com/features/workspaces/) - **Plugins**: install categories and rules made by the community into a workspace from the plugin catalog, with a preview before anything changes. Only the catalog is downloaded; no workspace data leaves your server. `PLUGINS_ENABLED=true`. - **AI Agents**: self-hosted assistants over your data, multi-provider, with tool use and a per-agent knowledge base. [Guide](https://docs.usesecuro.com/features/agents/) ## AI-Assisted Development Parts of this codebase were built with help of AI. All code is human-reviewed and no data leaves your environment. Contributing with AI is welcome. We review the author, not the tool: whatever wrote the diff, you own its quality, its fit with where Securo is going, and everything that happens after it merges. See [Using AI](CONTRIBUTING.md#using-ai). ## Support Securo Securo is free and open source, and it runs entirely on your own infrastructure. If it helps you, a coffee keeps development going:

## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for setup and guidelines. Not sure where to start, or want to talk something through first? [Book 15 minutes](https://cal.com/tassio/15min) — no agenda needed. Something broken, an idea, or just what you think of Securo, all welcome. ## License This project is licensed under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0](LICENSE). This means you can freely use, modify, and distribute this software, but any modifications — including when used as a network service (SaaS) — must also be released under the AGPL-3.0.

releases.name: v0.18.0
releases.body: In this release we added category splits: one transaction can now be divided across several categories, by amount or by percentage, and each part counts in its own category in budgets, reports, the dashboard and the category filters, while the account balance and the card bill still use the whole amount. Splits also work on recurring bills and installment series, so every generated occurrence starts already split, and they survive CSV export and import, the backup and the built-in MCP server. The MCP server can now read the investment ledger too. On the fixes side, a card or loan in credit counts as money you hold in net worth, deleting a group settlement removes the transactions it wrote, and a user who wrote invoices can be deleted without taking the workspace's billing records with them. ## Features - **Split one transaction across several categories,** by amount or percentage, with a badge in the list and "part of" rows in the dashboard drill-down. Closes #425 (#1383, #1387, #1392) - **Split recurring bills and ins

releases.name: v0.17.0
releases.body: In this release we added contract tracking for financing and loans: a mortgage, a car or other financing, a student or personal loan can now be tracked for its whole term, with the real contract behind it. Give it the amount, the rate, the term, the first payment and the amortization (Price or SAC), and Securo works out the payment schedule, splits the next payment into interest and principal, and shows when it will be paid off, both on the contract's terms and at the rate you are actually paying it down. You can break a recorded payment into principal and interest against the property it pays for, turn a bank-connected account into one of these, and enter the balance the lender reports so an indexed or renegotiated contract keeps matching it. We also added monthly budget rollover, surplus analysis and a multi-month forecast, a one-click suggestion of budget limits from earlier months, net cash-flow bars in Reports, a dashboard chart that compares a month against earlier ones, and more ways for the built-in MCP server to propose edits. On the fixes side, both sides of a group split now see the same balance, projections count only your share of a split, and open connections survive

releases.name: v0.16.6
releases.body:
In this release we added a loan account type that links to a property and shows the equity left on it, a System theme that follows the operating system, and a reworked date range selector in Reports with month presets, period navigation and a year picker. Agents can now be started from a template instead of a blank form, a selection of transactions can be acted on from a context menu, and a pending row can be marked as posted in one click. On the fixes side, cash a bank auto-invests is no longer counted twice, an asset in a currency with no rate stays out of the primary-currency totals instead of being passed off as converted, group balances are computed from who actually paid, and a SimpleFIN access URL keeps syncing its healthy accounts when one bank behind it needs reauthorization.

## Features

- **Loan accounts linked to a property.** A loan can name the real-estate asset it is secured against; the expanded property lists its loans with the debt and the equity left, and the dashboard shows loans as their own row instead of folding them into the available balance. Refs #344, by @eilandnl (#1055) 🎉
- **A System theme that follows the OS.** The theme button now steps Light, Dark

releases.name: v0.16.5
releases.body:
In this release an import stops guessing when it hits a cell it cannot read, and tells you which rows it skipped and why. Reauthorising an Enable Banking connection no longer duplicates the accounts it already imported, a closed account keeps its history in the period reports, and a balance in a currency with no rate is shown in its own currency instead of being passed off as converted. Securo can also be installed as an app now, Transactions and Reports remember the range you were looking at, and the new transaction form asks which account you mean instead of picking one for you.

## Features

- **Install Securo as an app.** A web manifest with its icons, so the browser offers to install it and it opens in its own window. Closes #1052, by @jacklu97 (#1068) 🎉
- **Transactions and Reports remember the date range.** The range survives a reload and moving between pages, and each report tab keeps its own. Closes #1053, by @rogeriocamorim (#1130) 🎉
- **The new transaction form asks which account.** It used to preselect one, so a transaction could land on the wrong account without anyone choosing it. Closes #1114, by @patouinparis (#1194) 🎉
- **Hong Kong dollar and New Taiwan dollar.*

releases.name: v0.16.4
releases.body:
In this release Securo speaks Hungarian and Czech, the cash-flow report names the day your balance runs out, and the transaction form starts suggesting descriptions you have used before. The rest is a round of fixes, most of them from reports: a credit card's detail page no longer reads its utilisation from a stale balance, an amount typed with comma decimals keeps its cents when repeated as installments, the onboarding tour's buttons stay inside their card, and a bank sync can no longer return the same transaction on two pages while hiding another.

## Features

- **Hungarian.** The whole interface, all 2572 strings. By @gergohajzer (#1123) 🎉
- **Czech.** All of it too, with the plural forms the language needs. By @Ajtak with @jakub-klik-it (#1149) 🎉
- **Cash flow says when the balance runs out.** The report now carries the lowest point of the projection and, when it crosses zero, the day it does. It is read off a day by day walk, so a dip inside a month still counts when the chart is drawn by month. By @rhuanbarreto (#1030) 🎉

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source, self-hosted personal finance manager designed for complete data sovereignty.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Securo is a privacy-focused personal finance and budgeting application designed to run entirely on user-controlled infrastructure. By keeping the platform self-hosted, it prevents third-party corporations and advertisers from accessing or analyzing sensitive financial data. The platform aggregates bank account information, tracks spending habits, and visualizes overall financial health through a comprehensive dashboard. It is available via a simple installation script and is strictly licensed under the AGPL-3.0 to ensure transparency. Ultimately, it provides a secure alternative to popular cloud-based budgeting applications that monetize user data.
keyFeatures: Self hosted infrastructure: Runs entirely on your own servers or home lab to guarantee complete data sovereignty.
Comprehensive dashboard: Visualizes spending habits, account balances, and financial trends in a clear interface.
Privacy focused architecture: Prevents the transmission of personal financial data to any third-party analytics engines.
Open source transparency: Licensed under AGPL 3.0, ensuring the codebase remains transparent and auditable.
Easy deployment: Offers a simple curl-to-bash installation script for quick setup on compatible systems.

useCases.title: Managing personal budgets
useCases.description: Users track their monthly expenses and income streams securely without relying on commercial SaaS products.

useCases.title: Consolidating financial data
useCases.description: Individuals bring multiple account histories into a single unified view hosted safely on a home server.

useCases.title: Enhancing data privacy
useCases.description: Privacy advocates ensure their sensitive financial records remain strictly confidential and off corporate servers.

useCases.title: Analyzing spending habits
useCases.description: Users categorize and review historical transactions using built in tools to make better financial decisions.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Securo is built for privacy advocates, home lab enthusiasts, and individuals demanding granular control over their personal finances. It appeals strongly to users who distrust commercial finance applications that monetize user data.
